newsitem.title: USA: John Dorrance weighs selling Campbell shares.
newsitem.headline: John Dorrance weighs selling Campbell shares.

text.p: John Dorrance, heir to the Campbell Soup Co fortune, said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission he intends to make "additional dispositions" of his shares in the company "when economically advantageous."
Dorrance, who is a citizen of Ireland, said he intended to make the sales "as opportunities became available."

Dorrance, who retired from the Campbell board in 1995 after 10 years of service to the company, said such dispositions "may be substantial." He currently holds a 9.5 percent stake or 23,405,246 shares, the filing showed.
According to a previous filing, Dorrance's stake was reduced to that level after his recent sales of 3.486 million Campbell shares at prices ranging from $72 to $77.375 a share.
Those shares sold constituted about 14 percent of his stake before the sales, according to the previous filing.

In today's disclosure, Dorrance also said he currently intends not to participate in Campbell's recently announced buy back of 18 million shares in a Dutch auction self-tender offer. A Campbell spokesman said that no directors or major shareholders under a voting trust will be participating in the tender offer.
The spokesman said that Dorrance, like other shareholders of the company, "are free to do what they wish with their holdings."
"We are focused single-mindedly on building the value of the company, which builds the wealth of every shareowner," the spokesman added.
